followUps.text: Consolidate the two remaining primary mintToken client copies (src/pages-modules/multiplayer/multiplayerPage.helpers.ts with its lobby/spectate callers, and the local copy in src/pages/multiplayer/index.tsx) onto mintCoopCredential or a shared helper. Named under hard invariant 11; no registered unit owns them.

Three small rules live in presentation because localSeatCredentialStore.ts is frozen: (1) the choice-to-seat-id mapping (choice === seat1 ? local-seat-1 : local-seat-2) is in LocalSeatCredentialPanel.tsx and in the store mint body; (2) the renewal-window and expiry classification is in the CoopCredentialRenewal view (it uses the store RENEWAL_WINDOW_MS, so no number is duplicated); (3) the join-time "never replace a match bearer with a different identity" guard in CampaignCoopEntryPanel.tsx mirrors replaceCoopCredential IDENTITY_CHANGED. Follow-up: the store exports seatIdForChoice, a renewal-state classifier and a join-time bearer-adoption guard, and the panels call them.

At entry, the IDENTITY_CHANGED message says to forget the sign-in and reclaim through co-op entry, but the only per-match forget control is inside CoopCredentialRenewal, which renders nothing while the bearer has more than four minutes left (pinned by LS16). In the same tab a user who rejoins a match with a different credential has no reachable forget until the window opens (workaround: a new tab). Fails closed; not a security issue.

The reviewer variant P15 (LocalSeatCredentialService.mint reports seat 1 playerId for seat 2) is KILLED by LS21a distinctness and LS21c; closure should record it beside the L2-M20 variant, which is killed by a mint refusal.

receiptQualifications.text: LS13 pins that a bad stored choice is never used, not that it falls back to primary. The frozen store throws INVALID_CHOICE with "Forget it and choose again"; the chooser is disabled with that message, a join refuses with the same message and mints nothing (pinned by the join test added after review), and "Forget next-join choice" returns the choice to primary. A silent display or mint fallback would substitute the primary GM identity for a profile that chose a seat. Reviewer ruling: acceptable, no admission amendment needed; record as a qualification at closure.
